section_summary: This section brings together State Department discussions of economic policy toward Japan, reparations, postwar controls and the division of responsibility for planning. It also contains letters proposing approaches to occupation and reconstruction, reports on Japan’s wartime economy, and a Chungking despatch transmitting translations of Japanese periodicals. The final document, a translated article advocating a Japanese controlled economy and national currency, continues beyond page 56.

subfiles.title: Letter on Canadian trade policy and other bilateral matters
subfiles.about: Parsons discusses Canadian commercial policy, a fisheries quota, Canol talks and Canadian payments.
subfiles.summary: Parsons describes a possible dispute over U.S. agricultural export pricing, the allocation of a groundfish quota, forthcoming Canol discussions and Canadian payments to the War Department.

subfiles.title: Conversation on research into Japan’s industrial development
subfiles.about: Officials compare available research for a study of the historical growth of Japanese industry.
subfiles.summary: O. R. Johnson seeks studies of Japan’s industrial growth for comparison with the United States and Russia and for estimating China’s prospects. Participants identify work on national income, shipping and other topics.

subfiles.title: Transmission of Economic Policy Toward Japan: Summary Statement
subfiles.about: Haley sends a provisional economic policy paper for area committee comment.
subfiles.summary: Requests comments on a provisional economic policy paper to expedite its submission to the Executive Committee.

subfiles.title: Copy of memorandum transmitting Economic Policy Toward Japan
subfiles.about: A second copy transmits the provisional policy paper for comment.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate transmission asks the area committee to comment on the provisional economic policy paper.

subfiles.title: Routing note enclosing Mason’s comments
subfiles.about: Haley reports sending the policy paper to Blakeslee and encloses Mason’s comments.
subfiles.summary: Reports transmission to Blakeslee and forwards Mason’s comments.

subfiles.title: Comments on Economic Policy Toward Japan
subfiles.about: Mason criticizes the paper’s lack of a clear vision for postwar Japan.
subfiles.summary: Mason questions the paper’s political assumptions and inconsistencies, while allowing its circulation for discussion.

subfiles.title: Responsibilities for economic studies on Japan
subfiles.about: Lockhart urges clarification of responsibility among committees studying Japanese economic policy and reparations.
subfiles.summary: Lockhart reviews overlapping work by the Far Eastern Area Committee, a reparations group and the new ECA Committee on Japan. He proposes circulating the broad economic policy paper to clarify their respective roles.

subfiles.title: Holdcroft letter concerning peace proposals for Japan
subfiles.about: Holdcroft forwards a missionary statement opposing lenient treatment of Japan.
subfiles.summary: Holdcroft rejects another missionary group’s plea for leniency and argues that militarism and State Shinto must be dismantled. He asks Grew to consider the enclosed statement.

subfiles.title: Missionary Statement re Peace Proposals for Japan
subfiles.from: J. Gordon Holdcroft and other signatories
subfiles.about: Missionaries argue that Japan’s National Shinto military government cannot secure a lasting peace.
subfiles.summary: The statement disputes a call for a lenient peace, associates National Shinto with militarism and persecution, and lists missionary and mission board signatories.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment to Holdcroft
subfiles.about: Grew acknowledges Holdcroft’s letter and enclosed statement.
subfiles.summary: Acknowledges the statement and thanks Holdcroft for supplying the signatories’ views.

subfiles.title: Request to draft reply to Holdcroft
subfiles.about: The office requests a draft reply for Grew’s signature.
subfiles.summary: Requests a reply to Holdcroft’s letter for Grew to sign.

subfiles.title: Japanese economic conditions in occupied territories
subfiles.about: An airgram summarizes a newspaper account of Japan’s economic organization across occupied territories.
subfiles.summary: The account contrasts an integrated northern economic bloc with more isolated southern territories. It discusses transport, agriculture, raw materials, shortages, money circulation and armaments production.

subfiles.title: Area Committee attitude toward economic policy paper
subfiles.about: Lockhart reports Ballantine’s views on the policy paper and committee jurisdiction.
subfiles.summary: Ballantine favors using the paper as basic guidance while preparing separate answers to specific Army and Navy questions.

subfiles.title: Information on Yoshio Kora
subfiles.about: English recommends Yoshio Kora as a potentially useful contact for reconstruction.
subfiles.summary: English describes Kora’s engineering background and his skepticism toward Japanese militarism and emperor worship.

subfiles.title: Reply to Horace B. English
subfiles.about: Ballantine acknowledges the biographical information on Yoshio Kora.
subfiles.summary: Thanks English and says the information will be shared with relevant government offices.

subfiles.title: Transmission of English’s letter to the Secretary of War
subfiles.about: The State Department forwards English’s letter for the Civil Affairs Division.
subfiles.summary: Encloses English’s biographical account of a Japanese subject.

subfiles.title: Proposal to introduce English as Japan’s language
subfiles.about: A correspondent proposes making English Japan’s national language after surrender.
subfiles.summary: The writer argues that English would reduce barriers between Japan and the Western world and increase American influence.

subfiles.title: Reply concerning English language use in Japan
subfiles.about: Dickover responds cautiously to the proposal to replace Japanese with English.
subfiles.summary: He notes practical limits to imposing a language, citing Korea and the Philippines.

subfiles.title: Dooman’s comments on Economic Policy Toward Japan
subfiles.about: Lockhart records Dooman’s concern that the policy paper lacks detailed instructions.
subfiles.summary: Dooman broadly agrees with the paper but wants supplementary guidance for specific military government questions.

subfiles.title: Handwritten Far Eastern Affairs file note
subfiles.about: A brief handwritten note appears to concern the Sovereign correspondence that follows.
subfiles.summary: Handwritten file note; most wording is illegible in the OCR.

subfiles.title: Aladdin Company proposal for postwar rebuilding
subfiles.about: Sovereign asks about financing large scale reconstruction with prefabricated Aladdin houses.
subfiles.summary: Sovereign encloses a 1941 letter to Japan’s ambassador and seeks government financing or advice for rebuilding bombed cities in Japan and elsewhere.

subfiles.title: Aladdin Company letter to Ambassador Nomura
subfiles.about: The company offers to supply houses for Japanese cities after a possible war.
subfiles.summary: Sovereign promotes the company’s prefabricated houses, suggests U.S. financing for rebuilding Japanese cities, and asks Nomura to pass the proposal to Japanese officials.

subfiles.title: Hugh Miller’s offer to advise on postwar Japan
subfiles.about: Miller offers knowledge of Japanese contacts and politics for postwar planning.
subfiles.summary: Drawing on conversations in Japan in 1936, Miller proposes identifying Japanese leaders for a liberal government. He favors using the emperor’s prestige temporarily and offers to serve in an advisory capacity.

subfiles.title: Reply to Hugh Miller
subfiles.about: Miller is directed toward military government offices that might use his knowledge.
subfiles.summary: Suggests contacting Army, Navy or civil affairs training officials and supplying biographical information on Japanese figures.

subfiles.title: Draft reply to Hugh Miller
subfiles.about: An alternate draft thanks Miller for offering his Far Eastern expertise.
subfiles.summary: Thanks Miller and says the department is considering postwar Far Eastern questions.

subfiles.title: Area Committee discussion of controls over Japan
subfiles.about: Lockhart records debate over the duration and wording of postwar economic controls.
subfiles.summary: Committee members debate how long controls on Japan’s capacity to wage war should extend beyond occupation and how to distinguish successive policy periods. They also discuss electric power and import controls.

subfiles.title: Area Committee discussion of Japanese property and reparations
subfiles.about: Lockhart reports debate over private property rights in reparations policy.
subfiles.summary: Members revise reparations wording to avoid a disputed legal issue about private property.

subfiles.title: Draft clause on Japanese property abroad
subfiles.about: A draft authorizes sequestration of Japanese property abroad while deferring compensation decisions.
subfiles.summary: Addresses Japanese property in Korea, Formosa and former mandated islands, with protection for small individual holdings.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck forwards English’s letter
subfiles.about: Hornbeck forwards English’s letter from London for departmental attention.
subfiles.summary: Forwards English’s account and suggests acknowledging receipt.

subfiles.title: Hornbeck’s acknowledgment to English
subfiles.about: Hornbeck acknowledges the information on Yoshio Kora.
subfiles.summary: Says he is forwarding English’s letter to the Office of Far Eastern Affairs.

subfiles.title: Japanese periodicals on Japan’s war economy and other subjects
subfiles.about: The embassy transmits translations of twenty Japanese periodical articles.
subfiles.summary: The despatch lists translations on wartime economics, labor, food, resources, finance and personnel. It says future translations will be mimeographed and sent to the department.

subfiles.title: The Establishment of Japan’s War Economy
subfiles.from: Ryōkichi Nagai; translated by Jean Wang
subfiles.about: Nagai argues for restructuring Japan’s wartime economy around state issued currency and control of concentrated capital.
subfiles.summary: The article presents the war as a struggle against Anglo American capitalism and calls for political and economic changes to increase Japanese fighting strength and attract support in China and India. Nagai proposes replacing reliance on taxes and public loans with state issued currency backed by national productive capacity and managed distribution. He also advocates controlling monopolistic financial capital while retaining productive private enterprise. The translation continues after page 56.
